label: early original-phase token (t=2-5) after a prefix rich in s/z/w/l/n, strongest on x
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (98.9% of mass), at positions t=2-5 (97% of mass; peak t=3), never at t=0-1, at the delimiter, or meaningfully in the copy phase. It requires the preceding inputs to include several of s, z, w, l, n (also k, b weakly); the first token and the token two back matter as much as the previous one. The current input modulates it: x is by far the strongest (lift 6.8x; every top example is x at t=3 after an s/z/w/n prefix, e.g. s z w [x]), followed by l, f, c, r, n, digits 0/1. It is weak or absent when the current token is itself one of the prefix letters, and it is suppressed by digits in the prefix. The behaviour looks like a graded sum of prefix-token and current-token contributions, so a boolean predicate captures it only partly (dev F1 0.47, mass recall 0.63).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: in_tok=x (+2.99), prev2_tok=l (+2.53), prev2_tok=s (+2.44), prev2_tok=n (+2.43), prev2_tok=w (+2.42), prev3_tok=l (+2.30). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-5.53), prev2_tok=- (-5.52), in_tok=k (-4.87), in_tok=j (-4.05).
